chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Mu'ammar ibn Khallad, from Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) who said:
'It is befitting for the man that he extends provision to his dependants, lest they wish for his death.'
[And he recited this verse:] 'And they give food out of love for Him to the poor and the orphan and the captive' [76:8].
He said: 'The captive is the man's dependants. It is befitting for the man, when there is an increase in bounty, that he increases upon his captives in the extent of their provision.'
Then he said: 'So-and-so — God bestowed bounty upon him, but he withheld it from his captives and gave it to so-and-so, so God took it away.' Mu'ammar said: And that so-and-so was present.

key_terms.أسير/أسراء: Captive(s) — here reinterpreted by the Imam as household dependants, drawing on Quran 76:8
key_terms.السعة: Capacity/abundance — the level of provision and comfortable living standards
key_terms.النعمة: Bounty/blessing — divine gifts and material provisions from God
key_terms.عيال: Dependants/family members — those under one's financial care and responsibility

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Ridha say about a man's duty to provide for his family?
ai.summary: Imam al-Ridha (peace be upon him) teaches the obligation of generosity toward one's household dependants, reinterpreting the Quranic word 'captive' (asir) as referring to one's own family members. The Imam warns through a real-life example — witnessed by the narrator Mu'ammar — that withholding Allah's bounty from dependants results in its removal. This hadith belongs to a chapter on providing adequately for one's household.
word_analysis: there is an increase/he is given more
